title: VoiceFont Calibration Checklist
disclaimer: Use your own natural accent, not an imitation. These original prompts sample everyday sounds and delivery choices; they cannot capture every facet of a voice and do not test identity, emotion or pronunciation. Stay within a comfortable speaking range, take breaks and skip any task that feels uncomfortable. Record only your own voice or one you have explicit permission to use.

categories.title: Sounds in everyday words
categories.description: Natural word contrasts, vowels and consonants. Keep any distinctions or mergers that belong to your own accent.

categories.title: Connected speech
categories.description: Link words at your normal pace. There is no need to pronounce every written letter separately.

categories.title: Questions and emphasis
categories.description: Use meaning to shape the sentence. Capitals indicate a suggested focus, not extra volume.

categories.title: Comfortable variation
categories.description: Small, easy changes only. Never strain, shout, whisper forcefully or push to your limits. Every task here is optional.

categories.title: Expression and style pairs
categories.description: Read the same words with a different intention. Gentle acting is enough; skip anything uncomfortable.

categories.title: Everyday conversation
categories.description: Speak as if talking with someone you know. Use the supplied text so repeated recordings remain comparable.

categories.title: Repeat and consistency
categories.description: Repeat earlier words without trying to copy a waveform. Comfortable, ordinary delivery is the goal.

prompts.text: Please leave the green ticket beside the little blue tin.
prompts.instruction: Use your ordinary speaking voice.

prompts.text: The full bowl stood beside a cool pool of water.
prompts.instruction: Keep your own natural distinction between full and pool.

prompts.text: Sam packed a black bag and caught the last bus home.
prompts.instruction: Say this as an everyday observation; keep your natural a sounds.

prompts.text: We checked the wet deck before taking the late train.
prompts.instruction: Read smoothly without stretching the vowels.

prompts.text: A small pot of sauce was waiting near the door.
prompts.instruction: Use the vowel sounds that feel normal in your accent.

prompts.text: The nurse heard a bird while stirring her tea.
prompts.instruction: Keep or omit r sounds as you naturally would.

prompts.text: The bright kite rose above the quiet lane.
prompts.instruction: Read with easy movement through the vowel sounds.

prompts.text: Our neighbour found a brown pouch under the chair.
prompts.instruction: Do not imitate another accent.

prompts.text: Roy enjoyed the noise of coins dropping into the tray.
prompts.instruction: Keep a conversational pace.

prompts.text: Pat bought a pale blue boat for the pond.
prompts.instruction: Let p and b sounds stay clear without overdoing them.

prompts.text: Take the tiny dish to the desk by the gate.
prompts.instruction: Use a relaxed voice and ordinary consonants.

prompts.text: Five fresh flowers filled the vase by the window.
prompts.instruction: Do not force breath through the f and v sounds.

prompts.text: I think those three paths lead to the other side.
prompts.instruction: Use your natural pronunciation of th.

prompts.text: Sue chose a soft cushion with a silver zip.
prompts.instruction: Read naturally rather than as a tongue twister.

prompts.text: The usual measure of jam is a generous spoonful.
prompts.instruction: Keep the middle sounds in usual and measure relaxed.

prompts.text: Lily rarely leaves her red umbrella in the hall.
prompts.instruction: Keep your own r and l sounds; no imitation.

prompts.text: Mum hung the linen near the warm landing.
prompts.instruction: Read gently at an everyday volume.

prompts.text: We watched the quick young waiter carry the tray.
prompts.instruction: Let the words flow at your usual pace.

prompts.text: The crisp toast slipped from the plate onto the cloth.
prompts.instruction: Keep the clusters natural; do not exaggerate final sounds.

prompts.text: A careful photographer noticed a colourful butterfly.
prompts.instruction: Allow unstressed syllables to become lighter naturally.

prompts.text: Could you put it on the table when you have a moment?
prompts.instruction: Read as one polite request, with natural linking.

prompts.text: I would have called, but the train went through a tunnel.
prompts.instruction: Use the contractions or reductions that occur naturally while reading.

prompts.text: We are going to pick up a few things on the way back.
prompts.instruction: Use a normal conversational rhythm.

prompts.text: The bread and butter are in the bag next to the kettle.
prompts.instruction: Let small connecting words stay light.

prompts.text: First we checked the address, then we rang the bell.
prompts.instruction: Take an easy pause at the comma.

prompts.text: I left an orange and a note on the kitchen counter.
prompts.instruction: Link adjacent words however your accent normally does.

prompts.text: When the rain stopped, everyone stepped outside for a look.
prompts.instruction: Avoid separating every word.

prompts.text: It is a bit of a walk, but there is a bench halfway.
prompts.instruction: Read as a reassuring comment to a friend.

prompts.text: The parcel should arrive at about a quarter past ten.
prompts.instruction: Use an ordinary pace and natural t sounds.

prompts.text: If you need anything else, I will be just across the road.
prompts.instruction: Keep the conditional phrase connected and pause where comfortable.

prompts.text: Did you leave the window open?
prompts.instruction: Ask a genuine yes-or-no question, not an accusation.

prompts.text: Where did you put the spare key?
prompts.instruction: Ask as if you genuinely need the information.

prompts.text: Would you prefer tea, coffee, or a glass of water?
prompts.instruction: Offer three choices with natural list intonation.

prompts.text: You have already booked the tickets, have you?
prompts.instruction: Sound mildly curious. Use the question tune natural to you.

prompts.text: I thought you meant the small box.
prompts.instruction: Emphasise I: someone else understood differently.

prompts.text: I thought you meant the small box.
prompts.instruction: Emphasise small: the size was the misunderstanding.

prompts.text: We can meet on Friday if that suits you.
prompts.instruction: Emphasise Friday to suggest a different day.

prompts.text: We can meet on Friday if that suits you.
prompts.instruction: Make the invitation sound open and flexible, not insistent.

prompts.text: The path curves gently round the garden.
prompts.instruction: Use your normal comfortable pitch as a reference.

prompts.text: The path curves gently round the garden.
prompts.instruction: Use a slightly lower comfortable speaking pitch. Do not force it.

prompts.text: The path curves gently round the garden.
prompts.instruction: Use a slightly higher comfortable speaking pitch. No falsetto is needed.

prompts.text: I will put the clean cups on the shelf.
prompts.instruction: Speak softly but with voice, not a whisper. Skip if effortful.

prompts.text: I will put the clean cups on the shelf.
prompts.instruction: Use your normal indoor speaking volume.

prompts.text: I will put the clean cups on the shelf.
prompts.instruction: Project a little as if to someone across a small room. Do not shout.

prompts.text: We have time to check the map before we leave.
prompts.instruction: Speak a little slower than usual, keeping an easy rhythm.

prompts.text: We have time to check the map before we leave.
prompts.instruction: Use your ordinary speaking pace.

prompts.text: We have time to check the map before we leave.
prompts.instruction: Speak a little faster if comfortable. Clear speech matters more than speed.

prompts.text: There is a seat for you by the window.
prompts.instruction: Read plainly as factual information.

prompts.text: There is a seat for you by the window.
prompts.instruction: Sound gently welcoming, as if greeting a friend.

prompts.text: The little plant has grown a new leaf.
prompts.instruction: Read as a simple everyday observation.

prompts.text: The little plant has grown a new leaf.
prompts.instruction: Let a little pleasure show. A small change is enough.

prompts.text: We can try the other route in the morning.
prompts.instruction: Read plainly, without trying to persuade.

prompts.text: We can try the other route in the morning.
prompts.instruction: Sound calmly reassuring, not forceful.

prompts.text: I did not expect to find a letter in the box.
prompts.instruction: Give the information matter-of-factly.

prompts.text: I did not expect to find a letter in the box.
prompts.instruction: Add gentle surprise without gasping or raising your voice.

prompts.text: The meeting will begin after the short break.
prompts.instruction: Read like a clear, calm announcement.

prompts.text: The meeting will begin after the short break.
prompts.instruction: Say it casually to a colleague beside you.

prompts.text: The lid is still stuck, so I will leave it for now.
prompts.instruction: Read as neutral information.

prompts.text: The lid is still stuck, so I will leave it for now.
prompts.instruction: Suggest mild frustration with timing, not strain or loudness.

prompts.text: Hello, it is good to hear from you. How has your week been?
prompts.instruction: Speak as if starting a relaxed phone call.

prompts.text: Yes, that works for me. Shall I bring something for lunch?
prompts.instruction: Imagine replying to a friendly invitation.

prompts.text: Sorry, I missed the last part. Could you say the time again?
prompts.instruction: Make a polite request for clarification.

prompts.text: Let me think for a moment. I believe we turned left after the bridge.
prompts.instruction: Allow a short, natural thinking pause between sentences.

prompts.text: Thanks for waiting. The kettle took a little longer than I expected.
prompts.instruction: Speak as if returning with a cup of tea.

prompts.text: I see what you mean, although I would probably choose the smaller one.
prompts.instruction: Disagree gently at a normal volume.

prompts.text: For the soup, chop the carrot first. Then add it to the pan and stir slowly.
prompts.instruction: Explain these steps clearly to one listener.

prompts.text: The address is twenty-four Willow Lane, and the appointment is at half past two.
prompts.instruction: Read the numbers and time clearly, without exaggerated spacing.

prompts.text: I looked for the book upstairs. In the end, it was under the chair all along.
prompts.instruction: Tell this tiny story with an easy pause between sentences.

prompts.text: That is everything for today. Take care, and I will speak to you soon.
prompts.instruction: Close a conversation naturally.

prompts.text: Please leave the green ticket beside the little blue tin.
prompts.instruction: Repeat the first prompt in your ordinary voice. Do not try to imitate the earlier recording.

prompts.instruction: Ask the same genuine question again, without exaggeration.

prompts.instruction: Return to your normal pitch after the optional variations.
